comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Correction and critique, 2026-10-24. The description is wrong that msg post --to @human with no --group lands in a group of just that agent and the human: it goes to the one group they already share, which may hold others, is refused if they share several, and makes a pair group only if they share none (docs/cli/msg.md, Groups). The quick ask still works, without that guarantee. From the Codex critique, checked against the code: (1) Freeze the group, sequence number and author shown in the banner into its payload; today it carries only daemon and group (Notifications.swift:210), and each new message replaces the group's banner, so a reply resolved at callback time could go to whoever posted last. (2) A banner reply must not read the group: MsgRequest.Read takes only a group and moves the human's cursor to the head, so answering otter's banner would also clear heron's unseen question. Simplest first version: a banner reply leaves the read cursor alone. (3) @muster's banners are not replyable: @muster is never a valid addressee. (4) Keep the reply on failure and offer a way to recover it; never retry a post whose outcome is unknown.

creator: Alexander Terp
description: A banner for a message to the human says only how many wait and from whom ("2 messages for you from heron, otter", MessageNotification.body), so answering even a yes-or-no question means opening the transcript tab. Agreed in the Lectern page muster-group-conversation (2026-10-24) as the cheapest part of the group conversation work, and the one to ship first: the banner shows the newest message's text, and macOS's reply field posts the answer to that message's author, in that group, as @human, without bringing Muster forward. That gives agents a quick way to ask something small, with no new verb: msg post --to @human with no --group already lands in a group of just that agent and the human. What the daemon tells windows about messages waiting for the human carries counts and authors, not text, so it has to send the newest message's text as well.
title: A message banner shows what was asked and takes a reply
